body.text: A pinch with a thumb and a curled index finger can lift the housing and drive its pitch by changing the relative heights of the contact pads. I will test the contact geometry and its stability before distilling or fine-tuning a single observation-based network.

The CPU contact search produced a 370/384 randomized isolated lift rate. The first learned full-task policy reached the carry phase in dry runs, where the arm approached the column at palm x about 0.40 m. Move the destination farther forward and closer to the near edge of the goal zone, then check the path. Add the harness provenance key required by the checker. Optimize finger motion with explicit frozen-setpoint trials.

body.method: Recurrent MLP supervised on 150000 randomized observation and command states. The training teacher used optimized thumb/index grasp parameters, a fingertip inverse-kinematic pitch gesture and proprioceptive waypoint transitions. Optimization used AdamW and a held-out slice for pose, joint and transition diagnostics.
body.observed: In the left-view videos the hand descends with its fingers open and closes on the housing at about 4–5 seconds. One sequence ends during the following carry. In the longer failures the plug separates from the fingers and rests on the table below the hand. One housing tumbles before settling. The runner logs localize the common stop to column clearance on transport.

body.text: v2 removed every observed collision and passed check_deploy. The common failure is now loss of the plug in the turn. Train the turn while the arm holds still, carry only once it is stable, and measure both freeze trials. I am testing population search over complete contact motions alongside PPO on held-object reset states.

The first four-heading contact teacher had six full successes in 256 station episodes. Two canonical headings can exceed 70% on held-out CPU contact trials, but many grasps slip under lateral station-arm motion. A 3-finger grasp search now evaluates transport directly in the station. Isolated contact-Jacobian control of the original 2-finger grasp gave under 1% within 20 degrees after settling. I am using full station contact outcomes to select the next teacher.

The v3 CPU contact programs scored 201, 220, 188 and 106 successes in 256 independent local episodes per relative heading, but their full teacher scored only 6/768 in the station. The independent finger-only PPO teachers achieved both stability freezes and 10-degree uprightness in 19/1024 true-pose and 25/1024 partially observed isolated episodes, with zero full placements. The contact-Jacobian alternative retained about 13% after its rotation test. I am optimizing teacher postures directly in the full station dynamics, and screening a three-finger design with matched contacts on the sides of the housing. Neither PPO nor the Jacobian controller is in v3.

body.method: A recurrent MLP learns grasp selection, wrist approach, finger targets, motion rates and observation-conditioned phase transitions from four contact-optimized programs. Training mixes sampled anchor poses and 157742 station observation/teacher pairs. The teacher uses the true plug pose for the final wrist trim and lowering target.
body.observed: In the common drop video the fingers lift and pitch the housing, hold it on a corner, then leave it behind as the hand moves away. In the hardware-violation video the housing tilts during pickup, separates, and finishes blades down. The hand repeatedly moves back and forth after the drop. The evaluator measured an 80 ms loss of contact in that episode.
reward_terms: Local contact search used retained grip, finger-driven pitch, 20/40-degree freeze stability, upright table contact, hand clearance and release.
Supervised training used palm position, orientation, finger and motion-rate regression plus approach-family and transition classification.
domain_randomization: CPU contact search drew grip, friction, object mass, heading and approach perturbations. Two heading families included a lateral change of palm pose.
The station teacher and evaluation use the supplied physical and sensor distributions. The teacher picked its approach from a training-only IK sweep over position and yaw.

body.text: The carry-first station teacher for v4 completed 351/1536 full trials, with 630 episodes placing at some point, four hardware violations, and no stops. I am retaining the turn-first and CPU search checkpoints and reallocating their compute to carry-first coverage. The strongest short-start carry-first program reached 20/24 individual placements for a 315-degree relative heading. I am expanding it and the other stable grasps to neighboring headings, and evaluating a recurrent network that retains its target until its learned transition changes.

body.method: The recurrent network learns when to change its latent state from the palm and finger errors. It retains the entry observation for predicting goals and motion rates until the next event. The training-only teacher carries the closed three-finger grip to the zone before commanding the in-hand turn, and chooses among four relative headings.
body.observed: The failure video shows a successful pickup and transport. The hand holds the housing at an angle over the destination for several seconds. It loses contact near the end, and the housing finishes on its side. The successful video shows the housing pitching between the fingers, touching down in the zone, and remaining upright after the hand withdraws. The two held-setpoint copies in that success each moved 2.5 degrees.
reward_terms: Finger program search rewarded retention through lateral transport, in-hand pitch, stable 20 and 40 degree freezes, upright support and release, with costs for drops and hardware violations.
The final network was trained by supervised grasp and phase classification plus palm pose, joint target and action-rate regression.

body.text: The five-family carry-first teacher completed 487/1024 fresh full station episodes. A paired trial with a slower descent, a 24-degree wrist trim and an early surface-support event completed 485/1024 and caused three arm stops, so v5 retains the original descent. Initial heading perturbations up to 18 degrees caused small changes for several of the strong programs. v5 uses this measured tolerance in selecting a feasible approach. It adds heading-conditioned pose features and a trained neural residual-action readout.

The v5 full-range teacher succeeded in 1162/2048 episodes. At the end of the finger turn, the tracker was valid in 7.7% of episodes, so finger feedback and object-pose memory matter for trim and seating. A separate five-family teacher with dropout recovery achieved 512/1024 versus 487/1024 in the earlier baseline draw using the same seeds, with zero stops or violations. Only 7 of 255 episodes with a retry succeeded, so I am prioritizing reliable first attempts. Screening candidate grips conditional on approach yaw and relative blade heading in the full station. The ideal-wrist search was stopped after 65 generations with its candidates retained.

body.method: A recurrent neural policy learns an eight-way grasp choice, a reachable wrist heading, a pose basis conditioned on that heading, target joints, action rates and observation-triggered transitions. A neural motor readout predicts the next Cartesian and finger adjustments. Station labels use the pose tracker at approach and true object pose for training-only late wrist trim and seating.
body.observed: In the failure video the hand picks up the plug, rotates it while holding it between the fingers, and releases it standing. The first table contact is 18.6 degrees from upright, outside the 15-degree requirement. The plug then settles flat on its base. The two frozen copies moved 3.0 and 3.6 degrees. In the success video, the housing pitches through the grasp before the hand descends, releases and withdraws. It touched down 3.6 degrees from upright after a 116.1-degree relative turn, and remained standing.
reward_terms: The training contact searches rewarded transport retention, airborne finger turn, stable held-setpoint copies, upright touchdown and release, with penalties for drops and hardware violations.
The final network regressed palm and finger goals and rates and classified grasp and recurrent progress. Its motor readout learned bounded single-step updates from randomized motor queries.
domain_randomization: The station teacher ran 2048 full episodes with randomized starts, sensor observations, servo and contact physical parameters. Synthetic supervision covered 170000 additional initial positions, headings and latent states.

The new resting command increased residual arm motion despite 732 legal set-downs. Keep the original withdrawal while evaluating nearer rest poses. The first CPU rounded-housing cluster experiment used the wrong object body name, so its rounded-model results are discarded and the corrected model is being rerun.

A candidate that combines planar alignment with v8 direct grasps is also in full-station training.

components.name: Conditional finger-program search and paired candidate tournament
components.standalone: On 288 matched held-out training starts per family the original program success rates were 72.9%, 78.1%, 35.8%, 25.0%, 68.4%, 51.0% and 57.6% for headings 75, 300, 250, 135, 315, 90 and 270 degrees. The selected program rates in the same order were 75.3%, 78.1%, 49.0%, 25.0%, 68.4%, 68.8% and 61.1%. These screening results were used for selection. The separate 3072 full starts above measure the complete teacher.

body.method: The recurrent policy learns seven grasp programs selected from an expanded archive of actual station rollouts. It learns reachable headings, recurrent progress, hand configurations and motor updates, and uses encoder history to estimate the trim and placement actions.
body.observed: The failure video at seed 2600002 showed the plug rolling out of the pinch close to the table. It lost hand contact for 0.07 s and touched down at 81.4 degrees, despite passing both frozen-setpoint checks. The hand withdrew over a plug lying on its side. Successful seed 18262615 stayed in contact throughout a 93.3-degree in-hand turn, touched down at 3.8 degrees and remained upright after the hand withdrew.
reward_terms: The training contact searches rewarded transport retention, airborne finger turn, stable held-setpoint copies, upright touchdown and release, with penalties for drops and hardware violations.
The final network regressed palm and finger goals and rates and classified grasp and recurrent progress. Its motor readout learned bounded single-step updates from randomized motor queries.
domain_randomization: The direct teacher ran over 3072 complete starts with the station's full tracking, physical and servo randomization. Synthetic supervised goals covered the continuous starting position and blade heading.
The network received 170000 randomized synthetic approach, finger-goal and progress labels in each training run.

components.name: Three-finger grip search and earlier seeds
components.standalone: In a selected station validation batch, the optimized three-finger grip retained 87/96 through transport, with 32/96 also within its initial-angle stability threshold. The kinematic pinch initializer retained 311/768 short-start lifts, and the earlier optimized CPU grasp retained 370/384 local lifts. A grasp alone does not place.

body.text: The inward slide during planar alignment caused 48 station stops over 2048 complete teacher episodes. We retain the restricted pivot workspace while testing other grasps for outboard starts. The v8 rounded-housing teacher achieved 1033/1536, and the official v8 box policy achieved 44/64 fixed and 45/64 fresh. A learned held-object readout predicted the blade direction within 6.16 degrees on average before trim and 2.24 degrees before descent on held-out teacher episodes. We are refining the wrist goal using on-policy demonstrations of those two contact events.

body.method: The recurrent action network adds an auxiliary learned estimate of housing position, blade axis and contact flags from legal tracking and encoders. `True` simulated object states label this estimate during training. At deployment the same network computes all commands and uses its own internal estimate to refine the palm pose.
body.observed: The failure video at seed 2600006 showed a pickup followed by a loss early in transport. The plug rose 5.16 cm, lost contact for 0.08 s and touched down on its side at 7.36 s, outside the goal. The empty hand continued toward the placement. At success seed 146332105 the grip held throughout a 97.7-degree turn, touched down at 4.1 degrees and released cleanly. Both frozen copies passed in both episodes.

At successful seed 7762041 the hand turned the plug 93.8 degrees relative to the palm, touched down at 11.2 degrees and withdrew after the plug settled upright.

components.standalone: On the same 1024 randomized starts with the measured rounded housing and blades, the original v8 network completed 535 starts and the mixed-domain fine-tune completed 600. body.text: On 1024 matched complete starts, a contextual adjustment of the v6 grasp raised success from 706 to 735 with zero hardware violations and stops. Independent support during the lift and carry reached 729. We are testing whether these improvements combine with encoder-conditioned finger turns. The safer v10 pivot map without lateral withdrawal achieved 1250/1536 with zero stops and reacquired all 401 routed objects; the faster lateral withdrawal introduced ten column stops and gave no median time saving. The next hybrid uses the original withdrawal.
